lesson.title: Concavity: Reading the Bend in the Curve
lesson.summary: Concavity describes which way a graph bends: a positive second derivative means the curve bends upward like the inside of a bowl, a negative second derivative means it bends downward like a dome, and this bending is a separate property from whether the function is increasing or decreasing at the same time.
lesson.body:
A function f is concave up on an interval where f''(x) is greater than 0, and concave down on an interval where f''(x) is less than 0. Since f'' is the derivative of f', another way to say the same thing is: f is concave up wherever f' is increasing, and concave down wherever f' is decreasing. Concave up means the slope of the tangent line is itself getting larger as x moves right, so tangent lines rotate counterclockwise and the curve pulls away above them, forming the shape of a cup that could hold water. Concave down is the reverse: the slope keeps shrinking, tangent lines rotate clockwise, and the curve sags below them, forming the shape of a dome that water would run off of.

Return once more to f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 - 9x + 5. Its second derivative is f''(x) = 6x - 6 = 6(x - 1), which has a single zero at x = 1. Testing x = 0 gives f''(0) = -6, negative, and testing x = 2 gives f''(2) = 6, positive. So f is concave down on (negative infinity, 1) and concave up on (1, positive infinity). Because (x - 1) appears to the first power, an odd power, this is a genuine sign change, the same crossing behavior discussed in the section on sign change analysis, and it means the bend of the graph flips at x = 1, from sagging to cupping.

It is worth being careful not to confuse concavity with monotonicity. Monotonicity, covered earlier, is about the sign of f' and asks whether the graph is heading up or down. Concavity is about the sign of f'' and asks whether that heading is speeding up or slowing down, that is, how the graph bends while it travels. The two properties are independent: a function can be increasing while concave down, for example f(x) = sqrt(x) for x greater than 0, where f'(x) = 1 / (2 sqrt(x)) is positive so the function climbs, but f''(x) = -1 / (4 x^(3/2)) is negative so the climb keeps slowing down, the graph flattening out as it rises. Knowing both the sign of f' and the sign of f'' together gives a much sharper picture of a graph's shape than either one alone.
